inputs.text: Hey, this parent with three kids in the public schools is apologizing to the educators and staff at South Portland School District, saying it's beyond maddening to face another large budget shortfall that's forcing the loss of more than 70 positions. They feel the pinch as a taxpayer, but they're spot on that this stems from long-standing structural inequalities that starve public education while shielding the wealthy from contributing their fair share. These repeated cuts aren't neutral—they disproportionately harm working families, communities of color, and the most vulnerable students who count on adequately funded classrooms and protected educator jobs. We have to demand real institutional reform to prioritize labor rights and equitable funding instead of letting these crises keep repeating.

output.main_topic: A South Portland School District budget shortfall forcing the loss of more than 70 positions, framed as a consequence of structural inequality.
subtopics: Structural inequalities in public education funding
Calls for labor rights and equitable funding
